newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia PM to look at Morgan RBA gold sale role.
newsitem.headline: Australia PM to look at Morgan RBA gold sale role.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Thursday he would inquire into WMC Ltd chief Hugh Morgan's involvement in the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) decision to sell most of its gold reserves.
"I will be making some inquiries to inform myself," Howard told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
Morgan, WMC's managing director, is also a member of the central bank board.

"I don't know what happened at the Reserve Bank board meeting and I do think that any public comment on that should be dealt with by the governor of the Reserve Bank, because it does operate independently," Howard said.
Howard said the bank was independent and he would not comment further at this stage.
The bank announced on July 4 it had sold 167 tonnes -- or two thirds -- of its gold reserves over the previous six months.
Gold prices have since tumbled to a 12 year low.

WMC increased its gold hedging this year, with its hedge book rising to 3.04 million ounces at June 30 from 727,000 ounces at the end of September, 1996, its latest quarterly report said on Wednesday.
The company's general manager of corporate development, Chris Leptos, said the hedging strategy was set in May 1996 after a review of WMC's worldwide gold operations.
The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported on Thursday that Morgan was present during the Reserve board's gold sale discussions.
